body.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the pretreatment rank-\(r\) fit satisfies
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n).
\]
For every fixed \(|h|\le q\), decomposition into the oracle residual-product average, two signal-error cross terms, and a quadratic signal-error term gives
\[
 |\widehat\gamma(h)-\gamma(h)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}
 +\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2\right),
\]
and hence the same bound holds for \(\Delta_\gamma\).
body.proof_tex:
On \(I\times S\), treatment is absent by \(\mathrm{ass:window\mbox{-}after\mbox{-}preperiod}\), \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\), and causal consistency. Thus
\[
 Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{I\times S}=M_{I\times S}+\epsilon_{I\times S}.
\tag{33}
\]
The preperiod Gram lower bound and exact rank imply
\(\sigma_r(M_{I\times S})\ge c\psi\). Applying the trace-moment calculation (3) to the full preperiod rectangle gives
\[
 \|\epsilon_{I\times S}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{n\ell_n})=o_{\mathbb P}(\psi).
\tag{34}
\]
Use the resolvent expansion (16)--(17) for \(\mathcal P_r\) at \(M_{I\times S}\). The rowwise linear term is the sum of a rank-
\(r\) projection of one noise row and a left-space average across independent rows. From (2), finite \(q\), and a union bound over \(N=O(n)\) rows,
\[
 \max_{i\in I}m^{-1/2}
 \|[D\mathcal P_r(M_{I\times S})\epsilon_{I\times S}]_{i,S}\|_2
 =O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n/\sqrt n).
\tag{35}
\]
The rowwise versions of (16)--(17), (34), and the signal envelope bound the quadratic and integral terms by \(O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n)\). Combining this with (35) proves
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{fit}}le C_{\mathbb P}\ell_n^2/\sqrt n.
\tag{36}
\]

Put \(d_{is}=\widehat M^{\mathrm{pre}}_{is}-M_{is}\) and define the oracle product average
\[
 \widetilde\gamma(h)=\{N(m-|h|)\}^{-1}
 \sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{s:s+|h|\in S}\epsilon_{is}\epsilon_{i,s+|h|}.
\]
The products have a fixed dependence range no larger than \(2q+|h|\) and uniformly bounded sub-exponential moments by (2). Coloring time into a fixed number of classes and applying the exponential Markov inequality to the product moments gives
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma(h)-\gamma(h)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}\right)
\tag{37}
\]
uniformly over the finitely many \(|h|\le q\); this bound is conservative because it does not use the additional pooling over \(N\).

Expanding \(\widehat e_{is}=\epsilon_{is}-d_{is}\) gives exactly
\[
 \widehat\gamma(h)-\widetilde\gamma(h)
 =-\overline{d_s\epsilon_{s+|h|}}
  -\overline{\epsilon_s d_{s+|h|}}
  +\overline{d_sd_{s+|h|}},
\tag{38}
\]
where each bar denotes the same normalized row--time average as above. Cauchy--Schwarz, (36), and the uniform boundedness in probability of the average noise square yield
\[
 |\overline{d_s\epsilon_{s+|h|}}|
 +|\overline{\epsilon_s d_{s+|h|}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}),
 \qquad
 |\overline{d_sd_{s+|h|}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2).
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (37)--(39) prove the claimed covariance rate and, because \(q\) is fixed, the maximum-lag rate.
